WITH fielding_players AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT f.player_id, p.bats
  FROM fielding f
  JOIN player p ON f.player_id = p.player_id
),
hand_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    bats,
    COUNT(*) as count
  FROM fielding_players
  GROUP BY bats
),
totals AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(count) as total_count,
    COUNT(*) as num_hands
  FROM hand_counts
)
SELECT 
  hc.bats,
  hc.count,
  CAST(hc.count AS FLOAT) / t.total_count as share,
  hc.count - (CAST(t.total_count AS FLOAT) / t.num_hands) as above_avg
FROM hand_counts hc
CROSS JOIN totals t
WHERE hc.count > CAST(t.total_count AS FLOAT) / t.num_hands

assumptions.assumption: Each player has a single, consistent bats value in the player table. Fielding records are joined to players to retrieve this value, and a player with multiple fielding records is counted once per batting hand.
Players with NULL or blank bats values form their own group and are included in the hand grouping and average calculation.
